target_customer: Small and mid sized teams managing shared cloud app accounts
problem: Teams shared passwords insecurely and struggled to add or remove employees across dozens of cloud apps.
business_model: freemium SaaS tiers up to 199 dollars per month
product_category: password sharing and single sign on for cloud apps

founders.name: Boris Jabes
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; he later co-founded Census.

founders.name: Anton Vaynshtok
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

founders.name: Bradley Buda
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in TechCrunch's acquisition report and as a former founder on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrations with about 1,500 cloud apps and single sign on, built by a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: App connectors give some lock in, but identity vendors could and did compete on the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: LogMeIn bought Meldium in September 2014 and then bought LastPass in October 2015, folding the technology into that product.

market_need_then: Cloud app sprawl made shared logins and offboarding a growing pain for small teams; Meldium connected to about 1,500 apps including Google Apps, Dropbox, Salesforce and Zendesk.

branding.domain_note: meldium.com now hosts an unrelated business and finance blog.

brand_strength.rationale: Only acquisition coverage and directory entries were found; no brand pages or community.

outcome_analysis: Meldium sold password sharing and single sign on to small teams and was bought by LogMeIn in September 2014 for 15 million dollars in cash, part of it tied to performance and retention. LogMeIn wanted identity features and later merged the technology into LastPass, so this was a strategic exit for a small team within two years of founding.
notes: The price was paid to BBA, the entity Meldium was incorporated under, per TechCrunch. An aggregator (startupintros, seedtable) reports a 1M seed round in July 2013 with no investors named; unverified so not recorded as a round. CB Insights shows 1.02M over 6 rounds, unreliable. Competitor search returned only aggregator lists (LastPass, OneLogin) with no source dated near the batch, so the list is empty. No source explains the name. Original site is dead and now an unrelated blog.
